headline: Four Seasons Casablanca Reports Record RevPAR in Q1 2026
summary: The Four Seasons Casablanca achieved its highest ever quarterly RevPAR of MAD 3,200 in Q1 2026, driven by strong corporate demand and a surge in Gulf state visitors. The luxury property saw occupancy reach 84%, outperforming the national luxury segment average by 12 percentage points. Management attributed the result to a new Gulf-focused sales strategy and the continued growth of Casa Finance City as a regional business hub. The property is now outperforming comparable assets in Dubai and Riyadh on a RevPAR-per-key basis.
body:
The Four Seasons Casablanca recorded a Q1 2026 RevPAR of MAD 3,200 — its highest quarterly result since opening — representing a 22% year-on-year increase versus Q1 2025.

Occupancy for the quarter reached 84%, versus a national luxury average of 72%, driven by a 40% increase in corporate bookings from Gulf-based financial institutions and a record volume of transient leisure guests from Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

The property's ADR of MAD 3,810 also reached a new record, reflecting the hotel's decision to reduce OTA exposure and push direct and consortium rates. The revenue management team shifted a further 12% of room nights to negotiated corporate rates at above-average ADR, insulating the property from seasonal softness in March.

Casa Finance City continues to anchor corporate demand for the property. With over 20 international financial institutions having established regional headquarters in the district since 2022, the Four Seasons Casablanca has become the de facto conference and lodging venue for the Gulf-Africa financial corridor.

HIQ analysis: At a trailing 12-month RevPAR of MAD 2,940, the Four Seasons Casablanca is now the highest-performing individual hotel asset in the HIQ database. The property's performance validates the investment thesis for ultra-luxury positioning in Casablanca, and is likely to accelerate competitive development in the Casa Anfa and Marina districts.
author: HIQ Editorial

headline: Marriott International Opens Autograph Collection Hotel in Marrakech Medina
summary: Marriott International has officially opened the Riad Dar Salam Marrakech, Autograph Collection — a 68-key boutique luxury property embedded within a restored 18th-century riad complex in the Marrakech Medina. The opening marks Marriott's first Autograph Collection property in Morocco and signals a broader push by international chains into the experiential luxury segment. The property required a seven-year restoration and represents an estimated MAD 320 million investment by the Casablanca-based owner, Almaz Hospitality Group.
body:
Marriott International has formally opened the Riad Dar Salam Marrakech, Autograph Collection, a 68-key boutique property occupying four interconnected riads in the northern Medina quarter, near Bab Doukkala.

The property joins Marriott's Autograph Collection — a portfolio of independent hotels selected for their distinctive character — and represents the brand's first entry into the Moroccan Medina segment. Existing luxury competition in the Medina is dominated by independent maisons and the Royal Mansour Marrakech, which remains the clear market leader.

The opening follows a seven-year restoration of the 18th-century riad complex, led by Moroccan architect Aziz Moussaoui in collaboration with the Marrakech Medina heritage authority. The project was financed by Almaz Hospitality Group, which retains ownership under a long-term management agreement with Marriott.

At an opening rack rate of MAD 4,200 per night for a garden suite, the property positions itself firmly in the Luxury segment and above the existing Medina boutique average of MAD 2,800. HIQ estimates a stabilised year-one occupancy of 68–72% based on comparable Medina openings, implying an opening-year RevPAR of approximately MAD 2,940–3,024.

The property features 68 keys across four room categories, two restaurants, a hammam and spa, and a 400-square-metre private event courtyard. A rooftop bar with Atlas Mountain views is scheduled to open in September 2026.

HIQ view: The Autograph Collection entry into Morocco's Medina segment is significant. International brand distribution will widen the property's reach beyond the European leisure market that currently dominates Medina demand. Competitors should expect rate compression in the upper tier of the independent boutique segment.
author: HIQ Editorial

headline: ADIA Acquires Minority Stake in Three Moroccan Luxury Resorts Valued at MAD 1.8 Billion
summary: The Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) has completed the acquisition of a 35% minority stake in a portfolio of three Moroccan luxury resort assets — the Amanjena Marrakech, Palais Namaskar Marrakech, and a greenfield site in Agadir — in a transaction valued at approximately MAD 1.8 billion. The deal is the largest single foreign direct investment in Moroccan hospitality real estate since 2019 and signals renewed Gulf appetite for trophy assets in the kingdom's leisure market. The transaction was structured as a joint venture with the existing Moroccan owner, Groupe Alliances.
body:
The Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) has finalised the acquisition of a 35% minority stake in three Moroccan luxury hospitality assets, in a transaction advised by CBRE Hotels and Lazard.

The portfolio comprises the Amanjena Marrakech (32 keys, Luxury), the Palais Namaskar Marrakech (41 keys, Ultra Luxury), and a 4.2-hectare greenfield development site in Agadir's Taghazout Bay resort corridor, entitled for a 120-key ultra-luxury resort expected to open in 2029. The combined transaction value is estimated at MAD 1.8 billion, implying a blended cap rate of approximately 5.2% on in-place NOI from the two operating assets.

ADIA will acquire its stake through a newly created joint venture vehicle, Najm Hospitality Partners, alongside existing owner Groupe Alliances, which retains a 65% controlling interest and day-to-day management oversight. No change to brand affiliations is anticipated.

The deal is the largest disclosed foreign direct investment in Moroccan hospitality real estate since Accor and CDC acquired the Risma platform in 2019 and reflects the continued internationalisation of Morocco's luxury hotel investment market. GCC sovereign and institutional capital has accelerated its deployment into North African hospitality since 2023, drawn by improving asset yields, currency stability, and Casablanca's ambition to position itself as a gateway financial hub.

HIQ analysis: The implied MAD 1.8 billion valuation — approximately MAD 24,700 per key on the operating portfolio — is a new benchmark for luxury hospitality real estate in Morocco and sets a reference for other trophy asset owners. The Taghazout Bay site inclusion indicates ADIA's conviction in the Agadir-Taghazout resort corridor as a long-term growth market, consistent with Morocco's Vision 2030 tourism investment roadmap.
author: HIQ Editorial
